brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A long-established green tea from around Jieting and Huangjinping in Guanzhuang, Yuanling County, Hunan.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It flourished in the Tang dynasty and was offered as tribute. Its making changed after 1949 from a twice-rolled, twice-baked method to a part-baked, part-pan-fired one. The craft is listed as intangible heritage in Hunan.
processing: Traditionally rolled twice and baked twice; since 1949 finished by a mix of baking and pan-firing.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Plump, tight strands of emerald green with visible white down.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Clean aroma and a strong, full taste with a lingering sweetness.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
